what: the compile-time guard that a new selector cannot silently reuse another's drawing
note: One case, killed by the **compiler** rather than by an assertion, and that
is the point: `flutter test` cannot run a program that does not build, so
the harness reports the build failure as `killed`. The guard did its job
before a single test ran.
Flattening the version dispatch in #43 bought one copy of the six-arm
variant switch instead of one per selector, and paid for it by narrowing
the guard `avatar.js`'s port used to have. `_Drawing` buys it back: a new
selector must name the picture it draws, and one that draws differently
must add a value — which makes the variant switch non-exhaustive. `0.3.0`
is the first release that will hit this.
**A second case was written and deleted, and the deletion is the finding.**
Replacing `final drawing = switch (version) {…}` with a hardcoded
`_Drawing.v1_6_1` — deleting the guard outright — left all 937 tests green.
It is a survivor by construction rather than a gap: with exactly one
drawing in the enum, a switch that maps every version to it and a constant
that *is* it are the same program. The guard is **inert today** and goes
live the moment a second value exists, which is what the surviving case
above proves. Same shape as the hidden-state rows this repo marks inert —
recorded here so the missing case is a judgement and not a silent skip.
#45 is the release the paragraphs above were waiting for, and both
predictions held: adding `v1_10_1` to `_Drawing` made the index switch
non-exhaustive and the compiler forced the dispatch before a test ran; the
once-inert guard is now live, so the case above moved from adding a second
value to adding a third. The from/to were refreshed to the #45 tree in the
same change (a stale case exits non-zero, but only when someone runs it —
#45 found two other case files stale since earlier refactors).

cases.name: a third drawing exists and nothing dispatches it
